source.title: Beyond Components: Singular Vector-Based Interpretability of Transformer Circuits
source.authors: Areeb Ahmad; Abhinav Joshi; Ashutosh Modi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes and intervenes on singular directions in GPT-2 Small components, not neuron poles or explanations of individual neurons. It does not test any listed version; its results are related findings about an alternative unit of interpretability.
record.gate_note: The paper argues that attention heads and MLPs contain multiple functional singular directions, but reports no neuron-pole job counts, held-out tests of neuron explanations, automated neuron-explanation scores, InceptionV1 analyses, or neuron-based attribution graphs. The rows below record results on singular-direction masks and interventions as related findings only (versions none). Cited circuit findings are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study decomposes GPT-2 Small attention/MLP weight matrices into singular directions and learns masks over them; it never measures individual neurons, neuron-pole job shares, explanation held-out prediction, simulation scores, InceptionV1, or neuron-based attribution graphs. Its results concern a different unit (singular directions within heads), so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that GPT-2 Small heads and MLPs are not monolithic but contain sparse, interpretable singular directions that multiplex subfunctions. Sparse masks preserve task behaviour, and scalar interventions on gender directions flip pronoun predictions. They limit the claim to GPT-2 Small and benchmark tasks, and say causal mediation is not fully established.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SVD of augmented attention and MLP weight matrices, learned diagonal direction masks, and scalar interventions in GPT-2 Small; it does not use neuron-pole explanations or test explanations against held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by task dataset. Gender-direction intervention effects are reported for all versus selected directions and differ across prompt contexts; the paper also reports effects at multiple amplification scales in Table 5.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned masks keep about 3–9% of singular directions while reproducing GPT-2 Small task behaviour (KLD 0.13–0.23).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In GPT-2 Small, sparse subsets of weight-matrix singular directions suffice to reproduce behaviour on IOI, GT and GP.

fits_no_version.finding: Single attention heads (e.g. 9.6, 9.9, 10.0) contain several singular directions with distinct interpretable roles (start-of-sequence, entity salience, entity/action separation).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention heads multiplex several interpretable subfunctions along orthogonal singular directions.

fits_no_version.finding: Swapping gender-direction activations with opposite-gender means and amplifying singular values flips pronoun logits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gender-related OV singular directions in GPT-2 Small causally steer pronoun prediction.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 (39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)
record.problems: The experiments cover GPT-2 Small and three benchmark tasks only; the authors state that generalization to larger models and instruction-tuned systems remains open. The authors also note that treating each matrix independently can obscure cross-component interactions, and that causal mediation is not fully established. Results do not directly evaluate neuron explanations or the listed neuron-pole claims.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted under the row limit. Direction-level token/activation examples and cited prior circuit results were not cataloged as outcomes for the listed claim versions.

record.verdict_notes: The paper uses 'superposed' for computations within heads, not neurons, and makes no claim about neuron monosemanticity. Its finding that units multiplex functions concerns heads, not neuron poles. It neither supports nor challenges V1–V7.
